why_angle: The cited results are all Renogy kit and inverter-charger listings. None of them gives the roughly 234 A that a 12V 3,000 W all-in-one draws from the battery, or says how many 100 A-BMS or 150 A-BMS LiFePO4 batteries it needs. This page works that figure out for every candidate and names a battery bank that can carry it.

page.answer: Short answer. The best 12V all in one solar inverter charger is the ALLWEI 3000W 12V hybrid: built-in MPPT, 120V pure sine output, $599. At 3,000 W it draws about 234 A from a 12V battery, so run it on two 150 A-BMS or three 100 A-BMS LiFePO4 batteries.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Battery current. A 3,000 W load on a 12.8 V LiFePO4 bank draws 3,000 ÷ 12.8 = 234 A. That is before inverter losses, so the real draw is higher. On a 24 V (25.6 V) bank the same load draws 3,000 ÷ 25.6 = 117 A.
  • Batteries in parallel. A 100 A BMS lets one battery supply 100 × 12.8 = 1,280 W. To supply 234 A you need three in parallel (300 A), because two give only 200 A. A 150 A BMS gives 150 × 12.8 = 1,920 W per battery, so two (300 A) are enough.
  • Solar string. The ALLWEI accepts up to 20 A of PV current, so it only reaches its 3,000 W PV maximum from a string running at 3,000 ÷ 20 = 150 V or more. In practice that means panels wired in series.
  • Surge. ALLWEI rates the hybrid at 3,600 W for 5 s, which is 3,600 ÷ 3,000 = 1.2× its continuous rating. Renogy lists the REGO at 9,000 W peak (3×) and PowMr lists its 1200W unit at 3× rated.
  • Price. The ACOPOWER costs $1,298 − $599 = $699 more than the ALLWEI. The REGO and Rover Lite together cost $989.99 + $249.99 = $1,239.98.
  • Whole 3 kW system. ALLWEI ($599) plus two Vatrer 150 A batteries ($519.98) comes to $1,118.98. Sun Gold Power 24V ($401) plus two Redodo 24V 100Ah ($939.98) comes to $1,340.98.

The battery decides how much of the 3,000 W you get

Every 12V 3,000 W unit in the table needs about 234 A at full output. The inverter can't deliver more current than the battery's BMS will release. Here is what each battery can supply, from the makers' own pages:

  • Vatrer 12V 100Ah Group 24, 150 A BMS ($259.99). One battery supplies 1,920 W. Two in parallel give 300 A, which covers 234 A plus inverter losses, for $519.98. This is the cheapest bank here that carries the ALLWEI at full output. {buy:vatrer-12v-100ah-group-24-bluetooth-150a}
  • Redodo 12V 100Ah Self-Heating, 100 A BMS ($251.99). One battery supplies 1,280 W, so a 3,000 W unit needs three ($755.97). This costs more than the Vatrer pair. It suits banks that charge below freezing, because its heating pads switch on under 32 °F. {buy:redodo-12v-100ah-self-heating-lifepo4}
  • Vatrer 12V 460Ah, 300 A BMS ($1,049.99). Vatrer rates it for 3,840 W of inverter load, so it is the one-battery way to run a 3,000 W 12V all-in-one.
  • Sun Gold Power's own sizing. Its SGK-PRO3 kit pairs a 3,000 W 12V inverter with two LiFePO4 batteries, a 300 A DC breaker and 2/0 AWG cable. It never uses a single battery.
  • 24V alternative. The Redodo 24V 100Ah has a 100 A BMS, which works out to 2,560 W at 25.6 V. Two in parallel carry the Sun Gold Power 3000W 24V's 117 A with room to spare. {buy:redodo-24v-100ah-lifepo4-battery}

The charging side is limited the same way. The ALLWEI's 3,000 W of PV charging into a 12.8 V bank would mean about 234 A of charge current. ACOPOWER's own 12V 100Ah battery accepts 50 A of continuous charge, and its 200Ah accepts 100 A. Set the unit's battery charge current to what the bank is rated for.

Not recommended

A 3,000 W 12V all-in-one on one 100Ah battery. A 100 A BMS shuts off at about 1,280 W, so in practice you have a 1,200–1,300 W inverter. Redodo's Group 24 Bluetooth page says the battery is not suitable for high-power uses such as water pumps. Even ACOPOWER's 12V 200Ah battery lists only 200 A of maximum continuous discharge, which is below the 234 A its maker's 3000W/12V all-in-one draws at full output.
